stem: A container has one moisture reading immediately before irrigation. What can the technician conclude about dryback rate?
choices: One moisture value cannot establish a dryback rate; repeated comparable observations are needed to describe change over time.
The dryback rate is known because the reading was taken immediately before irrigation.
The media is too dry because any pre-irrigation reading represents the lowest moisture point.
The irrigation interval is confirmed as correct because the technician captured a pre-event value.
rationale: Dryback describes change over time, so a single reading shows only one point in that trajectory. To estimate or compare dryback, the technician needs repeated measurements collected under comparable conditions. One pre-irrigation value cannot by itself show how quickly the root zone lost water or whether the interval was appropriate.
